page: Microsoft Azure HB368-48rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv5 family, configured with 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this virtual machine provisions 448.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 9.33 GB of RAM per allocated core. Built for demanding computational tasks, it features integrated support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage capabilities.

Storage architecture is characterized by a substantial local NVMe SSD allocation measuring 15,875 GB. The server operates without discrete graphics processing hardware, focusing entirely on CPU and memory-intensive workflows. The presence of such a massive high-speed local disk footprint minimizes IO bottlenecks for data-heavy operations requiring fast scratch space.

From an efficiency perspective, the machine provides a high memory-to-core ratio alongside extensive solid-state storage capacity on dedicated execution resources. The trade-off lies in the constrained core count relative to the wider HBv5 platform, trading total thread parallelism for elevated per-core memory bandwidth and memory capacity. Furthermore, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The hardware configuration makes the HB368-48rs_v5 suited for memory-intensive high-performance computing, large-scale database operations, in-memory analytics, and data-intensive simulation pipelines requiring low-latency RDMA interconnectivity and fast local NVMe caching.
